articles.title: 'Their careers are at stake as well': Gautam Gambhir defends India's bowlers after defeat
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Mayank Yadav's fiery opening spell was one of the positives for India in their second T20I against the West Indies in Ranchi on Friday.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Mayank Yadav's fiery opening spell was one of the positives for India in their second T20I against the West Indies in Ranchi on Friday. The fast bowler regularly clocked speeds above 140 kmph and took two wickets off successive deliveries in the first over, dismissing Kamil Pooran and Shimron Hetmyer. He later bowled Rovman Powell with a delivery clocked at 149 kmph.Mayank finished with three wickets in three overs but conceded 36 runs at an economy rate of 12.00.Despite his early strikes, India failed to defend 249 as the West Indies chased down the target to win by six wickets.India head coach Gautam Gambhir said the match could not be judged by what happened in the opening over."I have played enough cricket to know that games are not decided in the first over. Obviously, the West Indies are a strong T20 side. We respect them, and we know how dangerous they are. Games are not won or lost in the first over. A game of cricket is won or lost by the way you play consistently over the course of 40 overs," Gambhir said at the post match conference.Gambhir also backed Mayank to continue bowling at his natural pace instead of holding back."A fast bowler should bowl like a fast bowler. He is not a slower bowler," he said."If you can bowl at 150 kmph, bowl at 150. If you can bowl at 120, bowl at 120. When you are playing as a fast bowler, it is your duty to bowl fast, like a fast bowler," he added."That is what he did today, and that is why he was successful," Gambhir said.'Their careers are at stake as well'Gambhir also spoke about the need for a better contest between bat and ball after another high-scoring match. He had earlier described the Guwahati pitch as a featherbed.Asked whether India wanted better pitches, Gambhir said he wanted conditions that gave both batters and bowlers a fair chance."Don't you want a good competition between the bat and the ball? Of course, we want what you want. If you want to see sixes and fours, we want to see that as well. If you want an even contest between bat and ball, we want that too."The bowlers are our bowlers. They are not foreign bowlers. Their careers are at stake as well. They have worked hard, just like everyone else in the dressing room. If there is an even contest between bat and ball, it will be good. We will get to see better cricket.”Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'Only openers' spots are permanent': Gautam Gambhir's clear message on India's T20 batting order
articles.summary: India head coach Gautam Gambhir has backed the decision to promote Shivam Dube to No.
articles.body: India head coach Gautam Gambhir has backed the decision to promote Shivam Dube to No. 4 despite the all-rounder failing to make an impact in the second T20 International against the West Indies in Ranchi.Dube scored seven off 10 balls before being dismissed by West Indies off-spinner Roston Chase. However, Gambhir said India would continue to change their batting order according to the match situation, adding that only the opening positions are fixed in T20 cricket.'Only the openers are permanent'Dube was promoted to No. 4 after Ishan Kishan's dismissal, with Shreyas Iyer coming in later. India backed Dube to take on the spin bowling despite Chase's success against left-handed batters."We have used him like this for a long time, including during the World Cup and before it. It is not as though this was a one-off decision today," Gambhir said at the post-match media interaction at the JSCA Stadium.India lost momentum in the middle overs after losing wickets in successive overs, including top-scorer Sanju Samson. Iyer and Tilak Varma, however, scored quick runs towards the end to take India to 249/5.Gambhir stood by the decision to send Dube in at No. 4 and said the team would continue to be flexible with its batting order."This is international cricket. Sometimes things go your way, and sometimes they don't."We lost momentum today, but we have also gained a lot of momentum by sending him in at No. 4, where he has taken on the opposition bowlers," the coach said."More importantly, I think we have always been flexible with our batting order, and we will continue to do that. I have always said since taking over that in T20 cricket, only the openers are permanent. The rest of the batting order should remain flexible.”Samson's 82 goes in vain as West Indies script record chaseIndia's total of 249/5 was not enough as the West Indies chased down the target in just 18.3 overs to level the five-match series 1-1. Samson led India's batting with 82, while Iyer scored 40 off 18 balls and Tilak remained unbeaten on 44 off 18 deliveries.Samson and Kishan added 97 runs for the second wicket. Samson reached his half-century in just 21 balls, while Kishan scored 43 off 22 deliveries before being dismissed by Chase. The off-spinner also removed Dube for seven. Samson's innings ended in the 15th over, but Iyer and Tilak provided late runs to help India post their highest-ever T20I total against the West Indies.West Indies had a difficult start to the chase, with Mayank Yadav taking two wickets in the opening over. However, captain Shai Hope and Sherfane Rutherford turned the match around with aggressive batting against India's spinners.Hope scored an unbeaten 102 off 45 balls, hitting six fours and nine sixes. Rutherford made 84 off 37 balls, with seven fours and seven sixes. The pair added 120 runs off just 54 balls to put the West Indies in control. Mayank dropped Rutherford, and the missed chance proved costly for India.Romario Shepherd then scored 34 off 13 balls to help the visitors finish the chase in 18.3 overs and level the series 1-1.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'Doesn’t make sense': Dinesh Karthik on scrapping Impact Player rule before IPL 2027
articles.summary: The Impact Player rule has remained one of the most debated aspects of the Indian Premier League, with questions over its influence on team strategies,
articles.body: The Impact Player rule has remained one of the most debated aspects of the Indian Premier League, with questions over its influence on team strategies, high-scoring contests and India's ability to develop quality all-rounders. Royal Challengers Bengaluru's batting coach and mentor Dinesh Karthik has acknowledged the rule's shortcomings but believes the IPL should retain it for the 2027 season before deciding its future.Karthik argued that removing the rule before the conclusion of the current IPL cycle would be unfair to franchises that have assembled their squads keeping the additional player in mind. While admitting that the rule has gradually lost its relevance, he stressed that any decision to discontinue it should be taken only after the completion of the ongoing cycle.Speaking to Cricbuzz, the former India wicketkeeper-batter explained why maintaining consistency in the tournament's playing conditions is crucial, even as concerns grow over the long-term impact of the rule.Dinesh Karthik explains why Impact Player rule should stay for IPL 2027"When it first came on (Impact Player rule), it was very good because there were high-scoring games and there were a lot of teams that were almost chasing it down. But strangely, this last season, there were not too many close games."It just felt like one team scored a lot, and another team ended up chasing it down. And if you look at how the impact player rule has impacted the IPL, it was quite positive at the start. But slowly but steadily, it started losing the charm and the reason why it was there," Karthik told Cricbuzz.He highlighted that the rule has made an impact on India not being able to produce many all-rounders. "It helped make the game more high-scoring than what it was. But it definitely decreased the chances of India as a cricketing country producing all-rounders," he said before wanting the rule to stay this season."But what I wouldn't want is it to be scrapped for this season because teams have been picked with having an impact player in mind. So it makes a lot of sense."When you pick a team, you're picking a team based on 12 players that you're going to play. Now suddenly if you make it 11, there could be a team which is obviously not as strong as a 12 but much better as an 11, and it is an unfair advantage, and it's something that they could do away with after the end of this season."But in general, I do feel it was quite good at the start, but right now it's losing the relevance and importance that it probably provided for the fans and for the players as well," he added.‘Doesn’t make sense’ to scrap rule mid-cycleKarthik further stated that a rule should be brought before the start of the cycle and scrapped after the cycle ends, consolidating his claim of why he wants the rule to stay until 2027, which will also bring curtains to the three-year cycle."But I just feel that, as a rule, whatever new rule you want to bring in, you need to bring it in at the start of a cycle and do away with it at the end of a cycle if you don't want to (continue). First of all, this impact player rule was brought in in between and then to do away with it in the middle of one, I don't think makes sense. That's all I would say," he added.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'Big assets for India': Robin Singh identifies key factor that makes Rohit Sharma, Virat Kohli crucial for 2027 World Cup
articles.summary: With the 2027 ODI World Cup less than a year away, Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli's recent form has strengthened their prospects of featuring in the marquee
articles.body: With the 2027 ODI World Cup less than a year away, Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli's recent form has strengthened their prospects of featuring in the marquee tournament. Former India all-rounder Robin Singh believes the two experienced batters will be valuable assets for the Men in Blue as they prepare for the global showpiece in South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia.Rohit has scored two centuries and a 92 in his last five ODI innings, while Kohli has registered a hundred and two half-centuries during the same period. Their consistency has made them strong contenders as India work towards finalising their World Cup combination.Speaking exclusively to IANS, Robin emphasised that their current form, fitness and experience would be crucial to India's campaign.‘They definitely will be a big asset’: Robin Singh on Rohit, KohliRobin believes that age should not be a concern for the two former India captains, given their recent performances and commitment to fitness."I think experience is one thing. But more importantly, I think it's their form that is important. And of course, you know, with age you have enough and more experience. So that's really not a problem. They know what to do," Robin told IANS."It's more about staying in the moment, staying fit and keeping playing well. I think they are doing that exceptionally well. So there are no complaints. They definitely will be a big asset to the Indian team," he added.Robin Singh backs Gambhir's World Cup planningIndia have been experimenting with different combinations in recent ODI series as head coach Gautam Gambhir and his support staff assess their options ahead of the 2027 World Cup. Robin said the team management would look to provide opportunities to players who fit its long-term strategy before finalising the squad."I'm pretty sure Gautam and his team members will have their formula. I am sure he has a way of what he would like to do in the World Cup. What type of players he wants for the World Cup," he said.He added that the upcoming assignments would be important for identifying the best combination for the tournament.Bhuvneshwar Kumar, Mohammed Shami's World Cup chancesRobin also weighed in on the prospects of experienced pacers Bhuvneshwar Kumar and Mohammed Shami returning to India's plans, particularly with the 2027 World Cup set to be held in seam-friendly conditions. He said both bowlers have done enough to earn consideration, although their selection would depend on the team's requirements."I think these two are excellent bowlers irrespective of their age. They have actually done enough to give themselves a chance to get back into the side. Both are really good bowlers, excellent bowlers," Robin said.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: A season of opportunities: The selection battles that could reshape India’s T20I side
articles.summary: INDORE: With the 2028 T20 World Cup more than two years away, the Indian team has enough time to experiment before picking the 'Final 15' best suited to
articles.body: INDORE: With the 2028 T20 World Cup more than two years away, the Indian team has enough time to experiment before picking the 'Final 15' best suited to the conditions in host nations Australia and New Zealand.It also presents an opportunity for those looking to break into the T20I side and those trying to hold on to their spots, as the focus will be on preparing the team for the ODI World Cup coming up in a year's time.This five-match series against the West Indies is immediately followed by a tour of New Zealand from Oct 22. With plenty of T20Is lined up, the team management has room to manoeuvre, assess its resources and identify better options than those currently available.While Abhishek Sharma's spot looks secure at the moment, the same cannot be said about his opening partner Sanju Samson, who is always under pressure to perform every time he walks out to bat. Breathing down his neck is Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, who has impressed every time an opportunity has come his way in recent months. Not to forget Yashasvi Jaiswal, a proven performer in the shortest format, who is now adding wicketkeeping skills to his repertoire in a bid to break into both white-ball teams.Samson, though, showcased his class in the second T20I against the West Indies with a 41-ball 82, silencing his critics, at least for the time being.Tilak Varma was not pleased when he was pushed down to No. 5 and, at times, No. 6 after the 2026 T20 World Cup. However, he is beginning to come to terms with the role and has produced impressive displays, be it his unbeaten 22-ball 51 in the Asian Games gold-medal match against Pakistan or an unbeaten 18-ball 44 in Ranchi. More importantly, he has allayed concerns over his strike rate and is scoring at a brisk pace.The seam-bowling allrounder's spot is likely to be keenly contested between Shivam Dube and Nitish Kumar Reddy. If Hardik Pandya remains fit, only one of them may make the cut, which makes the battle even more intriguing. Reddy's bowling is considerably stronger than Dube's, who conceded 30 runs in two overs in Ranchi, while the 23-year-old Hyderabad youngster's batting continues to improve with every outing, even though he has not featured in the series so far.With Jasprit Bumrah, Arshdeep Singh and Harshit Rana expected to be India's frontline pacers by Oct 2028, the others will be eager to stay in the mix. Mayank Yadav gave a good account of himself with a fiery spell, while his Lucknow Super Giants teammate Prince Yadav will be keen for an opportunity as well. The young pacers will aim to keep performing with one eye on Bhuvneshwar Kumar, who is set to return for the New Zealand series.In the spin department, Axar Patel and Washington Sundar, who is not featuring in the current series, appear to be best placed thanks to their growing value with the bat. Kuldeep Yadav and Ravi Bishnoi are the other contenders in the race for a spot.A belter on offerWhile coach Gautam Gambhir was highly critical of the pitches offered during the series and called for a better balance between bat and ball. In Ranchi, he said bowlers' careers were at stake after the West Indies chased down a target of 250 in the second T20I, the second-highest successful chase in the format.The surface became increasingly easier to bat on in the second innings as dew settled in, making it difficult for bowlers to grip the ball.Expect similar conditions in the third T20I at the Holkar Stadium in Indore, where the pitch is traditionally flat, the boundaries are significantly shorter than those in Lucknow and Ranchi, and dew is expected to play a major role.The venue has witnessed one 400-plus and three 330-plus ODI totals, while teams have crossed the 220-run mark twice in T20Is. Another high-scoring contest is therefore on the cards on Sunday.The Indian team arrived in the afternoon and, shortly afterwards, Gambhir and his support staff visited the stadium to inspect the pitch. They had a brief discussion with the ground staff before leaving, anticipating another run-fest on offer.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Liton Das returns as captain as Bangladesh announce UAE tri-series squad; mystery spinner earns maiden call-up
articles.summary: Liton Das is back in Bangladesh’s ODI side as captain, with the Bangladesh Cricket Board (BCB) announcing a 16-member squad for the upcoming tri-series in
articles.body: Liton Das is back in Bangladesh’s ODI side as captain, with the Bangladesh Cricket Board (BCB) announcing a 16-member squad for the upcoming tri-series in the United Arab Emirates, also featuring Afghanistan and Zimbabwe, on Saturday.The wicketkeeper-batter missed Bangladesh’s ODI series against Zimbabwe in July due to a calf injury but returns to lead the side in the tournament starting October 17. Tawhid Hridoy has been named vice-captain, while experienced all-rounder Mehidy Hasan Miraz retains his place in the squad.The tournament will provide Bangladesh with an opportunity to assess their resources as they build towards the 2027 ODI World Cup.Aliss earns maiden ODI call-upMystery spinner Aliss Al Islam is the notable new face in the squad, earning his maiden ODI call-up after impressing in domestic cricket. The off-spinner has taken 35 wickets in 19 List A matches and 60 wickets in 59 T20s. He has also represented Bangladesh in T20I cricket, making his debut during the Asian Games.Fast bowler Hasan Mahmud returns to the squad, while express pacer Nahid Rana misses out as he continues to recover from a side strain. Rana has been absent from international cricket since July and also missed Bangladesh’s historic Test series draw against Australia, the Asian Games and the ongoing one-off Test against Afghanistan.Liton was appointed ODI captain in July, taking over from Mehidy, whom the board wants to allow to focus on his all-round contributions without the additional leadership responsibility.Tri-series begins on October 17Bangladesh will open their campaign against Zimbabwe in Abu Dhabi on October 17 before facing Afghanistan on October 21. Afghanistan and Zimbabwe will meet on October 19, with the top two sides advancing to the final on October 23.Zimbabwe have also announced their squad, with Sikandar Raza set to captain the side. Tafadzwa Tsiga and Vincent Masekesa have been included in place of Innocent Kaia and Graeme Cremer, while fast bowler Richard Ngarava continues his recovery from a back injury.Kaia is recovering from a thigh strain but is expected to be available for Zimbabwe’s T20I series, Zimbabwe Cricket said in a statement.Bangladesh squad: Liton Das (c), Tawhid Hridoy (vc), Tanzid Hasan Tamim, Saif Hassan, Soumya Sarkar, Najmul Hossain Shanto, Musaddek Hossain Saikat, Mehidy Hasan Miraz, Quazi Nurul Hasan Sohan, Rishad Hossain, Tanvir Islam, Taskin Ahmed, Mustafizur Rahman, Hasan Mahmud, Shoriful Islam, Aliss Al Islam.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Australia vs South Africa: Matt Renshaw epic innings puts tourists in command
articles.summary: After nine years and 280 days, Matt Renshaw scores epic century to put Australia on top against South Africa and push his own case for a regular place.
articles.body:
Australia 390: Renshaw 190, Cummins 43; Mulder 4-68

South Africa 27-1: Markram 15*: Hazlewood 1-9

Matt Renshaw scored an epic first Test century in more than nine years to put Australia in control of the first Test in their highly anticipated series against South Africa.

After much talk about the issues among their ageing top order on day one, Renshaw ground out a majestic career-best 190 from 397 balls in Durban, emphatically pushing his case to be part of Australia's future.

The 30-year-old was born in Middlesbrough and was a childhood friend of England captain Joe Root - their fathers played together in English club cricket - before his parents left the UK for New Zealand and then Australia when he was seven.

As well as potentially match-defining innings, having dragged Australia from 124-6 to 390 all out, it was a statement knock from Renshaw who has had an in-out international career.

"I like him as a player," former Australia batter Simon Katich said on SEN Radio.

"When he first came in, I liked him as a player, even though others thought he was too defensive.

"I think that is what this team has needed and been crying out for."

Renshaw scored 184 in his fourth Test against Pakistan in January 2017 after being handed a debut aged 20, but averaged 19.41 across 10 Tests across two spells before being recalled earlier this year.

"A few years out of the team, I had the opportunity in 2023, you think [you're] never going to get the opportunity again," Renshaw said.

"When I hit the ball [to go to his hundred] I was screaming at it 'go, go, go'.

"It hit me all at once. It was pretty special."

Against South Africa, the left-hander hit only three boundaries on day one - he attacked only 14.2% of deliveries in making his first 50 runs, the lowest figure of the Australia's top order. A throwback innings continued as he left well throughout day two, largely scoring square or behind the wicket.

He extended his partnership with captain Pat Cummins in the morning session to 86 and then expertly controlled a stand of 134 with number 10 Nathan Lyon to frustrate and tire South Africa's bowlers.

Renshaw took the strike when needed, protecting Lyon from the pace of Anrich Nortje, but became increasingly aggressive to add boundaries and inflict further pain as the partnership grew.

He added a further 21 alongside number 11 Josh Hazlewood before falling in the first over after tea.

Does Renshaw knock solve Australia's top-order dilemma?

Renshaw's superb innings, and opener Ryan Rickelton's three-ball duck in the 8.4 overs before bad light halted South Africa's reply, has left Australia well placed to push for victory on a pitch that flattened out on day two, but is expected to take turn later in the Test.

This series has been eagerly anticipated, given it is a repeat of last year's World Test Championship final, which was won by the Proteas.

It is also the third in a possible 21 Tests for Australia before the end of the Ashes next summer and, while Renshaw has surely secured his immediate future at least, his knock does not alleviate all questions over the make-up of their side.

When he was recalled in August it was in place of Jake Weatherald as opener, but he was moved down to number five for this Test when Cameron Green was ruled out.

Nic Maddinson came in at the top of the order alongside Travis Head, giving Australia an 11th different opening partnership since the retirement of David Warner.

With Green, the regular number five, expected to return and Maddinson making a 33-ball duck on day one, a solution to their top-order struggles would be to move Renshaw up again.

That would reunite him with Head, who made the surprise move to opener to impressive effect in the Ashes - he flogged England for centuries in Perth, Adelaide and Sydney - but has also shown vulnerability in failing to pass 22 in his four innings since.

Equally, Renshaw could stay in the middle order and Green return for fellow-all-rounder Beau Webster, meaning Australia's hunt for a settled opening pair would continue.

"No idea," Renshaw said of the decision ahead. "That's well above my pay grade.

"Whatever is the best for the team is the one for me. I am not too fussed."

articles.title: ‘He is somewhat similar to me’: Virender Sehwag says Vaibhav Sooryavanshi is in his prime
articles.summary: Former India opener Virender Sehwag sees a bit of himself in Vaibhav Sooryavanshi’s fearless approach to batting, saying the teenage sensation is in his
articles.body: Former India opener Virender Sehwag sees a bit of himself in Vaibhav Sooryavanshi’s fearless approach to batting, saying the teenage sensation is in his prime and should get as many opportunities as possible to build a long international career.The 15-year-old has already made an impression in T20Is, scoring 246 runs in eight matches at a blistering strike rate of 186. Sehwag, who amassed 17,253 international runs during his career, believes Sooryavanshi’s attacking mindset is reminiscent of his own approach at the crease.“Sooryavanshi is in his prime, and his thinking is somewhat similar to mine, that of hitting right from the first ball. Now, it is about when he gets the opportunity and how many matches he plays for India,” Sehwag said during a discussion at the PHD Chamber of Commerce and Industry's annual session on Saturday.‘Performance matters’: Sehwag on Sooryavanshi’s ageThe former India opener also dismissed concerns over Sooryavanshi’s age, arguing that performances should determine a player's place once they reach the highest level.“Look, if you are playing in an age-category, it makes sense — if it's Under-19, your age should be under 19. But once you play the IPL or play for India, age doesn't matter.“A 38-or 40-year-old (Virat) Kohli is playing, and a 15-year-old (Vaibhav) Sooryavanshi is also playing. Then, performance matters,” Sehwag said.Sooryavanshi has featured in eight of India's 18 T20Is since joining the senior set-up, with competition for the opening slots remaining intense. Experienced Sanju Samson and Abhishek Sharma have been India's preferred opening combination in recent matches.Former India all-rounder Robin Singh has also backed healthy competition for places, stressing that young players need a sustained run but must be patient when others are performing well.“Sooryavanshi has enough and more talent. So, you know, even if he has to sit on a bench and wait it out, it's okay. But the others have done very well,” Robin told IANS.“It's good to have competition. It's good to have people beating down your neck so that you don't slip up with your performances,” he added.Sehwag backs India’s World Cup hopesSehwag also praised Shubman Gill for his recent batting exploits, including his second ODI double century, and backed India's bowling attack to play a decisive role at the 2027 ODI World Cup in South Africa.“Among our fast bowlers, we have Bumrah, who is the best we have. articles.title: Matt Renshaw's career-best 190 rescues Australia against South Africa in rain-hit Test
articles.summary: Matt Renshaw produced a career-best 190 to rescue Australia from a precarious position and guide them to 390 all out in the first innings of the opening
articles.body: Matt Renshaw produced a career-best 190 to rescue Australia from a precarious position and guide them to 390 all out in the first innings of the opening Test against South Africa. After Australia slipped to 84/4 on Day 1, Renshaw's marathon knock helped the visitors recover from a collapse and put the hosts under pressure in a rain-affected contest.Renshaw faced 397 deliveries, striking 21 fours and a six, as he anchored Australia's innings with crucial partnerships down the order. His efforts helped the visitors recover from 124/6 and post a competitive total.Renshaw, Lyon frustrate South AfricaAustralia resumed Day 2 at 187/3, but South Africa continued to make inroads through the morning session. Wiaan Mulder claimed two wickets and finished with figures of 4/68, while Pat Cummins added 10 runs to his overnight score before departing for 33. Renshaw, meanwhile, reached his second Test century off 204 balls, his first since scoring 184 against Pakistan in Sydney in 2017.With Australia reduced to 277/8 at lunch, Nathan Lyon joined Renshaw to produce a crucial ninth-wicket partnership. The pair added 134 runs off 283 deliveries, with Lyon contributing 27 from 92 balls.Renshaw went past 150 off 311 balls and continued to frustrate the South African attack before Marco Jansen dismissed Lyon leg-before-wicket. Renshaw eventually fell for 190, caught at slip off Simon Harmer, as Australia were bowled out for 390.South Africa lose Rickelton as rain interrupts playSouth Africa began their reply late in the day and lost Ryan Rickelton for a three-ball duck, caught off Josh Hazlewood. However, Aiden Markram and David Bedingham remained unbeaten on 15 and 12 respectively as the hosts reached 27/1 at stumps.Australia held a lead of 363 runs, but persistent rain continued to disrupt proceedings. Nearly 25 overs were lost on the opening day, while a further 14.2 overs were lost on Day 2.The series marks Australia's first tour of South Africa since the 2018 ball-tampering scandal. South Africa, the reigning World Test Championship holders, defeated Australia in the 2025 final.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Ranji Trophy: Kerala eye fresh start as they open against Jharkhand
articles.summary: Twenty years ago, Keenan Stadium watched MS Dhoni do something he rarely did: Open the innings in an ODI.
articles.body: Twenty years ago, Keenan Stadium watched MS Dhoni do something he rarely did: Open the innings in an ODI. Alongside Virender Sehwag, he tore into England’s attack and blazed his way to 96. International cricket never returned to Jamshedpur ever since. Ranchi, Dhoni’s hometown, took the spotlight, and the steel-town bastion of Jharkhand cricket went quiet.On Sunday, Keenan Stadium will be back in focus. As Ranchi was busy staging the India-West Indies T20I two days ago, Jamshedpur bagged the rights to host Kerala’s Ranji Trophy season opener against Jharkhand.Kerala begin the season under a new captain, Vishnu Vinod, and a new coach, former Goa batter Swapnil Asnodkar.“New season, new start,” says Kerala mentor Prashant Padmanabhan. “A solid coach, and a captain who showed his leadership chops in the final Ranji game against Goa last season,” he told TOI. “The pitch looks dry and may assist turn on Days 3 and 4, which is where Kerala’s experience comes in. We are banking on our two veterans, Jalaj Saxena and Aditya Sarwate.”KCA secretary Vinod S Kumar, though, wants the youngsters to share the load. He points to offspinner Vaisakh Chandran, who bowled exceptionally in the pre-season warm-up game in Hyderabad, taking 11 wickets.Interestingly, Vaisakh made a sensational Ranji debut against Jharkhand in 2022-23, taking five wickets in the second innings at Ranchi to help Kerala win.What followed was far from ideal. The Thiruvananthapuram native was weighed down by family worries after his father fell ill. A few IPL franchises had noticed him, and he went for trials two seasons ago. Then came a shoulder injury, his form tapered off, and he missed the last season.“He seems to have found his mojo. articles.title: ‘Working on my skills with Joshi, Paranjape sir’: Tanush Kotian ahead of Ranji Trophy opener
articles.summary: MUMBAI: Set to embark on another domestic season where he desperately needs to make a mark to break into the Indian team, Mumbai's off-spinning allrounder
articles.body: MUMBAI: Set to embark on another domestic season where he desperately needs to make a mark to break into the Indian team, Mumbai's off-spinning allrounder Tanush Kotian has been working with former India left-arm spinner and currently the spin bowling coach at the BCCI's Centre of Excellence in Bengaluru Sunil Joshi and former India batter Jatin Paranjape's coaching academy in Mumbai to "improve his skills."“I have been working on my skills with Sunil Joshi sir at CoE and also at the VPCC with Jatin Paranjpe sir. I think this game will be crucial for me to show my performance and get into the (India A) side,” Kotian told reporters at the Wankhede Stadium on Saturday, a day before Mumbai launch their campaign in the 2026-27 Ranji Trophy against Chandigarh here.Kotian explained that he has been trying to employ various angles, bowling at different speeds, and, as he showed in the Duleep Trophy in Aug, also bowling with the new ball. Opening the bowling in the first innings of the Duleep Trophy for West Zone against North Zone at CoE, the 27-year-old took four for 72 for West Zone against North Zone, and followed that up with four for 46 in the second innings, to finish the game with eight wickets for 118, even though WZ went down by 52 runs.“I have been using the crease now really well with the angles, bowling over the wicket, round the wicket against the right-handers and left-handers. I’m also working on which pace is effective on [which] wicket. And with the variations, I’ve developed my arm ball and the straighter one during practice, and have worked on my ability to bowl with the new ball. I bowled in the Duleep Trophy with the new ball. So, I think it will be more effective when I get the new, hard ball to work with on a surface," Kotian explained.One criticism against Kotian is that he doesn’t pick too many top-order wickets. “I think I have done a lot. I have taken a lot of top-order wickets, and I have a lot of fivers also in my bag. So, I don't have to prove to anyone that I have done well. But I try to keep it simple and give my best in them,” Kotian answered.It didn’t help Kotian that the last Ranji Trophy season was an underwhelming one for him- India A duty and an elbow injury meant that all could manage to play was three matches for Mumbai in the Ranji Trophy, in which he took nine wickets@32.77. In the quarterfinal at MCA-BKC against Karnataka, Mumbai’s bowlers failed to defend 325 in the fourth innings, with Kotian taking two for 77 in 21 overs. How disappointing was that? “ No, it wasn't disappointing. According to me, I bowled very well. I bowled 21 overs in that game. Catches were dropped (off my bowling), but that's a part of the game. I injured my elbow in the third match, after that, I got injured. My elbow was injured.After that, I wasn't even going to play the Ranji Trophy quarterfinals, but it was the team's call that they needed me in the knockouts. So, I took that call too. The team was pushing me to play. So, I tried and played. It didn’t show in the wickets column, but I think I bowled top-class stuff. If we had grabbed a few opportunities, I would have taken a fiver,” he said.Kotian grabbed the selectors’ attention during the 2023-24 Ranji season. As Mumbai went on to win the title, he was named player of the tournament for scoring 502 runs at an average of 41.83 and taking 29 wickets at 16.96. However, the spinner is yet to make his Test debut, though he spent time in the India dressing room after being added to India’s Test squad for the final two Tests of the 2024-25 tour of Australia.It must’ve hurt Kotian that Madhya Pradesh’s 33 year-old off-spinner Sarandh Jain was preferred to him for India’s Test tour of Sri Lanka in Aug. Masking his disappointment well, the boy from Vikhroli gave an apt response to the question of not getting picked for India despite a consistent show the the ball and bat in the last few seasons.“I am performing well, but there is no disappointment. I see how I can win my team by performing well in each and every match. And wherever I get an opportunity, whether it is India A or the Duleep Trophy, I look to showcase the talent that I have. Like in fielding, I try to give my 100 percent. So, I try to stick to my expectations. And if I get a chance, I will wait for that opportunity and when that opportunity comes, I will try to grab it,” he said.Recently, he did well for India A against Australia A as well. “It's important for me to keep performing in each and every game. I have been doing that, I have that mindset to perform in bowling and batting both aspects for the team, in any situation. I look to go out there and give my best each and every innings, and score and take wickets for my team as much as I can,” Kotian said.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: South Africa vs Australia: Matt Renshaw ‌strikes career-best 190 to guide Australia to 390 all out on day two of the ​first test
articles.summary: South Africa 27-1 in reply to Australia's 390 all out; Matt Renshaw and Nathan ‌Lyon add record 134 for ninth ‌wicket; Renshaw's 190 is highest by number five in tests at Kingsmead
articles.body:
The touring side had been in a precarious position at 124-6 on ​the opening day but Renshaw led ‌a fightback before bad light stopped play on Friday and continued his ​form into the second morning, reaching his second Test ton almost a decade after his first against Pakistan ​in Sydney in 2017.

The 30-year-old brought up ⁠his century off 204 balls ⁠with his 10th four and was 102 not out at lunch, alongside Nathan ‌Lyon on seven.

Renshaw, who was expected to open the batting but surprisingly dropped down the order to No 5, was 46 not out overnight and moved to his half-century with a boundary off the second ball of the day.

Renshaw shared an 86-run partnership with captain Pat ⁠Cummins, before the skipper got a thick ​edge to Wiaan Mulder and was ​caught at second slip by Aiden Markram for ​43.

Mulder bowled Mitchell Starc for six but by then ⁠Australia had added a healthy 43 runs to their overnight total of 187-6 as the pitch looked to ⁠have lost the bounce and movement ​of the first day.

Mulder was the pick of ​the home bowlers with figures of 4-51 off 22 overs and could complete his ‌first Test five-wicket ​haul after lunch.

articles.title: Vinay Kumar begins coaching journey as Karnataka begin Ranji Trophy campaign Andhra
articles.summary: VIJAYAWADA: Karnataka cricket and Vijayawada share a special connection, one that goes back nearly six decades.
articles.body: VIJAYAWADA: Karnataka cricket and Vijayawada share a special connection, one that goes back nearly six decades. It was here that a youngster from the erstwhile Mysore team announced himself to the cricketing world. GR Vishwanath’s storied career began with a sparkling 230 on his Ranji Trophy debut against Andhra here. In the same match, another Karnataka stalwart, VS Vijay Kumar, made his maiden foray into domestic cricket.On Sunday, as Karnataka begin their Ranji Trophy campaign against Andhra, the fixture will mark a few new beginnings. For R Vinay Kumar, the state’s last captain to lead them to the Ranji Trophy title, it will be the start of his full-time coaching journey.“It feels great to start my full-time coaching journey with my home team,” Vinay told STOI on the eve of the match.There will also be a first for R Smaran, who will captain Karnataka’s senior side for the first time in the absence of Devdutt Padikkal.Vinay believes the young left-hander has the makings of a good leader.“I’ve seen Smaran captain sides in domestic tournaments. Apart from being a good leader, he is also a shrewd captain. He ticks a crucial box by knowing the players well. With Dev and Smaran, Karnataka cricket is in good hands,” said the former India pacer.Karnataka, who last won the title in the 2014-15 season, came close to ending that wait last season before surrendering meekly to Jammu and Kashmir in the final on home turf.The challenge this time is complicated by the likely absence of their young batting mainstays, Padikkal and Smaran, at various stages because of national-team commitments.The pace department, meanwhile, has taken a significant hit. Injuries have sidelined four of the frontline quicks — Prasidh Krishna, Vyshak Vijaykumar, Vidwath Kaverappa and Vidhyadhar Patil, who has been ruled out for the season. The responsibility will fall on Abhilash Shetty, M Venkatesh, Manvanth Kumar and LR Kumar to step up.Vinay, however, sees an opportunity amid the setbacks.“We will miss our main pacers in terms of their experience and skill set. That said, their absence should be taken as a blessing in disguise to see how good your bench strength is,” he said.With Padikkal away on India A duty for the series against Australia A, Karnataka will lean on the experience of KL Rahul, Karun Nair and Mayank Agarwal. Smaran, too, will be keen to build on his recent form, having scored a half-century and a hundred against J&K, while representing Rest of India in the Irani Cup. The 23-year-old, though, will be looking for greater consistency after a mixed run of performances.Andhra, led by the seasoned Ricky Bhui, will be no pushovers. They have reached the quarterfinals five times since the 2019-20 season and are coached by Gary Stead, under whom New Zealand won the World Test Championship title. With a blend of experience and young talent, the hosts will look to make home advantage count.Karnataka, though, can draw confidence from their recent record against Andhra, having won three and drawn two of their previous five encounters.With temperatures soaring in the region and the pitch dry at the stadium in Mulapadu, the contest could hinge on spinners. Leggie Shreyas Gopal will lead Karnataka’s attack, with Shikhar Shetty and Ritesh Bhatkal in the mix.Hope the city that once served as the launchpad for a career that would go on to define Indian and Karnataka cricket becomes the starting point of something special for Vinay and his boys.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'Stupid boy': England cricket legend Ian Botham reignites feud with Ben Stokes
articles.summary: England cricket great Ian Botham has reignited his public feud with former England captain Ben Stokes, calling him a \"stupid boy\" and a \"has-been\" after
articles.body: England cricket great Ian Botham has reignited his public feud with former England captain Ben Stokes, calling him a "stupid boy" and a "has-been" after their disagreement over England’s Ashes preparations and Stokes’ retirement.Botham and Stokes, both regarded as among England’s finest all-rounders, have exchanged criticism over the past year. The dispute began when Botham questioned England’s preparations for the Ashes in Australia, arguing that the team should have played at least one state match before the series.Speaking to The Times Magazine, Botham criticised Stokes over the team’s approach and their decision to visit Noosa after losing the first two matches of the Ashes series. He said, "Stupid boy. I'll mention him only briefly because his self-indulgence is not something I enjoy."Although Botham praised Stokes as a great player, he questioned the team’s choices during the tour. Referring to their time in Noosa, he added, "Really? They were p****d as rats. Look, if you want a drink, don't go to the high street. We used to go to wineries."Botham had earlier said England’s failure to arrange a state match was a sign of arrogance, adding, "Not one (state match), which borders on arrogance. You've got to give yourself the chance."Stokes defended the team’s approach, pointing to changes in the modern game. He said, "There's quite a few factors that play into why we can't prepare how the has-beens maybe prepared in the past. The landscape of cricket has changed and that affects preparation."Stokes fires backAfter Stokes retired from England duty earlier this year, Botham mocked him during an appearance on Test Match Special. He said, "As we know Michael Vaughan and I, we don't know what we're talking about. Couple of old has-beens."Addressing Stokes directly, he added, "Ben, if you're listening, congratulations, you've joined the club - you're now a has-been."Stokes responded on X with a pointed remark, "The quote 'it's better to be a has-been than a never-been' originates from Lord Ian Botham."Botham has now taken another swipe at Stokes while releasing his new book, saying, "This is for you, Ben. articles.title: Two years to go, plenty to decide: India’s big questions ahead of the 2028 T20 World Cup
articles.summary: Indore: The 2028 T20 World Cup is still more than two years away.
articles.body: Indore: The 2028 T20 World Cup is still more than two years away. India have a valuable window to experiment before settling on the squad best suited to conditions in Australia and New Zealand, where they will defend their T20 crown. The extended build-up presents opportunities for established players looking to cement their places and those on the fringes to force their way into the side.With the focus likely to shift soon towards next year’s ODI World Cup, the current stretch of T20 cricket allows the team management to assess its depth and identify long-term options. The five-match series against the West Indies is followed by a tour of New Zealand from Oct 22, giving India ample scope to rotate personnel and evaluate talent.Abhishek Sharma’s place at the top currently appears secure, but the same cannot be said of his opening partner, Sanju Samson, who continues to face scrutiny every time he walks out to bat. Vaibhav Sooryavanshi has strengthened his case with a string of impressive performances, while Yashasvi Jaiswal, already a proven T20 performer, is adding wicketkeeping to his skill set in a bid to break into both white-ball teams.Samson, however, reminded everyone of his quality with a blistering 41-ball 82 in the second T20I against the West Indies, buying himself valuable breathing space. Further down the order, Tilak Varma has gradually embraced the middle-order role he initially resisted after the 2026 T20 World Cup. The left-hander has impressed with impactful cameos, including an unbeaten 22-ball 51 in the Asian Games final against Pakistan and an unbeaten 18-ball 44 in Ranchi. Most significantly, he has answered questions over his strike rate by scoring at a far more aggressive tempo.The contest for the seam-bowling allrounder’s slot could be one of the most intriguing. If Hardik Pandya stays fit, only one of Shivam Dube and Nitish Kumar Reddy may find room in the final squad. Reddy offers greater value with the ball, while his batting continues to progress despite him sitting out the current series.Among the pacers, Jasprit Bumrah, Arshdeep Singh and Harshit Rana appear to be the front-runners, but the race for supporting roles remains wide open. Mayank Yadav impressed with his pace and aggression, while Prince Yadav awaits his chance. Bhuvneshwar Kumar’s expected return for the New Zealand series adds another interesting layer to the competition.In the spin department, Axar Patel and Washington Sundar appear well placed because of their all-round value, while Kuldeep Yadav and Ravi Bishnoi remain firmly in contention.Another run-fest on the cardsWhile Gautam Gambhir criticised the pitches used earlier in the series and warned that bowlers’ careers could suffer on such batter-friendly surfaces, the third T20I is unlikely to offer them much relief. The Ranchi wicket became significantly easier to bat on under lights, as dew made life difficult for bowlers during the West Indies’ successful chase of 250.Similar conditions are expected at Indore’s Holkar Stadium, traditionally one of India’s most batting-friendly venues. With short boundaries and heavy evening dew forecast, another high-scoring encounter appears likely. The ground has already produced one 400-plus and three 330-plus ODI totals, while teams have crossed 220 twice in T20 Internationals.India reached Indore on Saturday afternoon, after which Gambhir and members of the support staff inspected the pitch and briefly interacted with the ground staff. All signs point towards another belter.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.body: Indore: Mayank Yadav cranked up some serious pace on Friday night, letting the ball fly and rattling the West Indies top order. No one in India’s think tank will get carried away after just one impressive spell, but there will be quiet satisfaction over what the Delhi pacer produced in Ranchi. His spell of 3/36, with all three wickets coming in the Powerplay, has reinforced India’s belief that in Mayank, they have an express pacer who can make an impact with the new ball and trouble batters in overseas conditions.The challenge, though, is to keep him match-ready and ensure his body does not break down. It has been a painful journey for Mayank, who first made his mark during the 2024 IPL with Lucknow Super Giants, consistently clocking speeds in excess of 150 kmph. The tearaway speedster played just four matches that season, but it was enough to convince the selectors that he needed to be fast-tracked into international cricket. By October 2024, he had made his India T20I debut against Bangladesh.What followed was an extended battle with injuries over the next two years, including a lumbar stress fracture, lower-back spasms and a hamstring tear. But the Indian team management knew they had a rare talent who needed careful handling. Under the guidance of VVS Laxman at the Centre of Excellence in Bengaluru, Mayank gradually rebuilt his fitness and bowling workload. He returned during the 2026 IPL but endured a quiet campaign. He made his India comeback during the Zimbabwe series in July this year and marked his return with a Player of the Match performance. What kept the fire burning was his desire to wear the India jersey again.Skipper Shreyas Iyer handed him the new ball, and Mayank delivered. More importantly, the pace was back.Coach Gautam Gambhir did not mince his words when asked about Yadav’s performance. articles.title: ‘Their careers are on the line too’: Gautam Gambhir’s blunt message after India’s bowling struggles
articles.summary: Ranchi: Roston Chase’s miserly spell of 3/24 in four overs was crucial in a run-fest in which 501 runs were scored in 38.3 overs, as West Indies stunned
articles.body: Ranchi: Roston Chase’s miserly spell of 3/24 in four overs was crucial in a run-fest in which 501 runs were scored in 38.3 overs, as West Indies stunned India by six wickets in the second T20I. On a surface that produced 249/5 for India and 252/4 for West Indies, Chase stood out with his ability to read the conditions and constantly change his lines. He removed three of India’s first four batters, briefly checking the hosts’ momentum before India recovered through their middle order.India head coach Gautam Gambhir highlighted Chase’s adaptability as the key to his success. “The way he altered his lines was very important because, on this wicket, changing your line matters a lot. Length may or may not change, but if you keep changing the line, you keep the batter guessing,” Gambhir said. “He bowled at the feet, went wide and bowled full. He kept mixing it up. On a wicket like this, that variation is extremely important.”The contrast was stark in the second innings. Express quick Mayank Yadav struck twice in the opening over as West Indies were reduced to 5/2 and then lost a third wicket in the Powerplay. But Shai Hope and Sherfane Rutherford turned the game around with a 120-run fourth-wicket stand off 54 balls. Hope finished unbeaten on a hundred, while Rutherford smashed 84 off 37 balls.Gambhir admitted the conditions made life difficult for the bowlers but insisted India could not use that as an excuse. “These are tough conditions for bowling. We know that flat wickets with dew make things difficult, but we need to figure out a way to stop the opposition,” he said.In a contest dominated by batting, Chase’s ability to remain economical and keep changing his angles provided a reminder that even on a belter, intelligent bowling can still influence the outcome. His 3/24 was not merely the best spell of the night; it was the spell that briefly brought control to a game otherwise almost entirely dictated by the bat.Bat-ball imbalance irks coach againThe defeat also brought Gambhir’s growing concern over the imbalance between bat and ball into focus. After India chased down a 400-plus target in fewer than 44 overs in the Guwahati ODI last week, he had said, “This is not cricket, this is batting.” In Ranchi, his assessment was along similar lines. “If you want an even contest, we want that too,” he said, adding, “Those bowlers are our bowlers. Their careers are on the line too. An even contest would make for better cricket.”Dube promotion fails to make an impactThe coach also defended the decision to promote Shivam Dube to No. 4, insisting it was part of a long-term strategy rather than a one-off move. Dube could manage only seven off 10 deliveries.“We’ve used him in that role for a long period, including before and during the World Cup. articles.body: In the age of the IPL and expanding state T20 leagues, the Ranji Trophy remains Indian cricket’s most prestigious red-ball tournament. Arunachal Pradesh will miss the first round, taking the number to 38 from the next round.The start of the season will have added star power, with Yashasvi Jaiswal turning out for Mumbai, KL Rahul for Karnataka and Washington Sundar for Tamil Nadu before they leave for the India ‘A’ shadow tour of New Zealand. Veteran allrounder Ravindra Jadeja will also be in action for Saurashtra. With India scheduled to play seven Tests over the next four months, two in New Zealand and five at home against Australia, the tournament carries extra significance for domestic performers hoping to push their case.Recent selections have shown that Ranji Trophy performances are being rewarded. Jammu & Kashmir swing bowler Auqib Nabi, who took 60 wickets in 10 matches last season, earned an India call-up. Left-arm spinner Manav Suthar, Devdutt Padikkal, off-spinner Saransh Jain and Karnataka batter Ravichandran Smaran have also benefited from strong domestic returns.BCCI secretary Devajit Saikia said the Ranji Trophy remains central to India’s talent pathway.“The Ranji Trophy is the premier domestic cricket tournament in India. All players who want to make a mark nationally and internationally have to take this tournament seriously because all eyes are on performances here,” Saikia told TOI.Saikia reiterated the BCCI’s policy that all available India players must play domestic cricket. “Whoever is available and not on national duty is mandatorily required to participate in the Ranji Trophy or other domestic tournaments,” he said. “It keeps senior players in rhythm and helps youngsters learn by sharing the dressing room with them.”Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.body: A teenage cricketer from Karachi, Pakistan, has caught the attention of cricket fans after scoring an impressive century in a school tournament. Interestingly, the left-handed wicketkeeper-batter shares his name with Australian cricket legend Adam Gilchrist, but his own cricketing hero is former Sri Lankan great Kumar Sangakkara.The young Adam Gilchrist plays for Kamran Public School in the Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) Talent Hunt School Cricket Championship Under-17 tournament. His recent performance has brought him into the spotlight, with a video of him explaining his name and favourite cricketer gaining attention online.Adam Gilchrist's match-winning centuryPlaying against Happy Palace Grammar School Karachi at Jinnah College, the teenager scored 117 runs off 108 balls. His innings included 11 fours, and he spent 145 minutes at the crease.His century helped Kamran Public School post a strong total of 297 for four in 40 overs. The best teams will progress through district and provincial rounds before the national finals.The initiative gives young cricketers an opportunity to showcase their skills and potentially take the next step in their careers.Why he was named Adam GilchristThe teenager's name has an interesting backstory. His mother selected the first name Adam, while his cricket-loving father added Gilchrist in honour of the legendary Australian wicketkeeper-batter.The original Adam Gilchrist played 96 Tests for Australia, scored 5,570 runs and was part of three World Cup-winning teams in 1999, 2003 and 2007. articles.title: ‘She is the best woman player in the world’: Will Sutherland on sister Annabel’s influence
articles.summary: Puducherry: For Will Sutherland, the road to mastering the nuances of Indian conditions has come with a familiar voice in his corner.
articles.body: Puducherry: For Will Sutherland, the road to mastering the nuances of Indian conditions has come with a familiar voice in his corner. His younger sister, Annabel Sutherland, one of the most accomplished allrounders in the women’s game, has been a guiding light as the Australia ‘A’ captain navigates the demands of international cricket.With Annabel having played extensively in India, the siblings have plenty of cricketing wisdom to exchange. “We talk about bowling and train with the same bowling coach. She has played over here a lot more, so we talk about conditions and that sort of thing. We definitely share a lot, which is awesome,” Will told TOI ahead of the third match.Their relationship, however, is not merely about exchanging technical notes. Growing up in a cricket-loving household, Will and Annabel, along with their younger brother Tom, turned their backyard into a competitive arena where sibling rivalry doubled as an informal training ground.“When I was younger, I could definitely bowl to her and she would smack it everywhere. There was a time when I didn’t have to hold back at all. She would try to bowl as fast as she could to me and Tom. Those battles probably helped us get a lot better,” he recalled.Annabel’s numbers underline why her advice carries weight. In seven Tests, she has scored 715 runs at an average of 89.37, including four centuries, besides claiming 19 wickets. Her 53 ODIs have yielded 1,087 runs and 67 wickets. She was also part of Delhi Capitals in the Women’s Premier League in 2025.While Will, who has played two ODIs for Australia, represents Melbourne Renegades, Annabel plays for Melbourne Stars in their respective Big Bash competitions. “I probably want the Renegades to beat the Stars, but I would wish Annabel well. I think she is the best woman player in the world.”As Will looks to establish himself as a genuine allrounder, Annabel’s advice has often extended beyond the nets. “She looks after her body a little better than me. She tells me to take a longer-term view because I want to play cricket for a long time. You cannot play every game. I want to be fit and healthy for March and April when IPL and other tournaments come around,” he said.The family’s cricketing conversations have deep roots. Their father, James Sutherland, formerly CEO of Cricket Australia, ensured that the game was never far from the dinner table. “Poor mum, all we talked about at dinner was cricket. We were lucky to travel around Australia and watch games with dad. Sometimes, as kids, we got to go into the change rooms and meet Australian players. That exposure motivated me to keep working,” he said.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Matt Renshaw eclipses Phillip Hughes, rewrites record books with 190
articles.summary: Matt Renshaw scripted a remarkable turnaround for Australia with a career-best 190 against South Africa in the first Test in Durban, registering the
articles.body: Matt Renshaw scripted a remarkable turnaround for Australia with a career-best 190 against South Africa in the first Test in Durban, registering the highest individual score by an Australian at the venue.Renshaw surpassed Phillip Hughes’ 160, scored in 2009, to claim the Durban record. His marathon knock also set a new benchmark for the highest individual Test score at the venue by a batter coming in at No. 5 or lower, eclipsing Sri Lanka’s Kusal Perera, who remained unbeaten on 153 in 2019.The left-hander faced 397 deliveries, striking 21 fours and a six, as Australia recovered from a precarious 84-4 on Day 1 and 124-6 to post 390 all out in their first innings.Renshaw found crucial support from the lower order, particularly Nathan Lyon, with whom he added 134 runs for the ninth wicket. Lyon contributed 27 off 92 balls in a stubborn partnership that frustrated the hosts for much of the second day.Renshaw brought up his second Test century off 204 balls, his first since scoring 184 against Pakistan in Sydney in 2017. He went on to reach 150 off 311 deliveries before completing his highest score in Test cricket.His innings also placed him among the highest-scoring Australians in South Africa in Tests. Greg Blewett’s 214 in Johannesburg in 1997 remains the highest, followed by Adam Gilchrist’s unbeaten 204 at the same venue in 2002 and Herbie Collins’ 203 in 1921. Renshaw’s 190 in Durban is fourth on the list.Marco Jansen eventually dismissed Lyon leg before wicket, ending the 134-run stand, while Renshaw continued to push Australia towards the 400-run mark. He was finally caught at slip off Simon Harmer, bringing an end to an innings that had rescued Australia from a difficult position.South Africa ended the second day at 27-1 in 8.4 overs, trailing by 363 runs. Ryan Rickelton fell for a three-ball duck to Josh Hazlewood, while Aiden Markram and David Bedingham were unbeaten on 15 and 12 respectively at stumps.Play was curtailed by rain and lost time for the second consecutive day, with 14.2 overs lost on Saturday after nearly 25 overs had been washed out during the final session on Day 1.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Rajasthan cricket seeks fresh start amid turmoil, faces tough Tamil Nadu test
articles.summary: Jaipur: Rajasthan cricket is more in the news for its off-field activities these days rather than actual performance on the ground.
articles.body: Jaipur: Rajasthan cricket is more in the news for its off-field activities these days rather than actual performance on the ground.With an ad-hoc body running the show for the last three years in the absence of a proper elected executive committee, cricket took a backseat.Finally Rajasthan Cricket Association (RCA) elections were conducted on Sept 29 but the Supreme Court stayed the declaration of the results, ordering that they be kept in a sealed cover pending further adjudication.Rajasthan’s newly-appointed captain Manav Suthar has a big responsibility to put all these things behind and inspire his teammates to perform to their best as they take on formidable Tamil Nadu in the Ranji Trophy opener at the Sawai Mansingh Stadium here on Sunday.The four-day Elite Group D fixture will be a big challenge for both the hosts as well as the visitors since most of the players are young and inexperienced.The two teams will face each other after a long gap of one-and-a-half decades. These two teams last met in the 2011-12 final in which Rajasthan won at the M A Chidambaram Stadium in Chennai.Tamil Nadu skipper R Sai Kishore will hope to provide a strong start to the season with a better performance in the season-opener.Tamil Nadu received a big boost with India allrounder Washington Sundar joining the squad on Friday. With S Sai Sudharsan doing India ‘A’ duties, skipper R Sai Kishore will be hoping the other batters make the most of the depleted bowling attack of Rajasthan.Experienced pacers Khaleel Ahmed, Deepak Chahar and Aniket Choudhary and leg-spinner Rahul Chahar are missing from the squad either due to injuries or rehabilitation.Left-arm spinner Mahav will be hoping to make the most of limited resources in the bowling department to counter the strong TN batting line-up. “The absence of regular bowlers will provide a golden opportunity for the youngsters to grab the chance and cement their place in the side. They have the potential and that’s why they are selected. Testing their abilities against a solid team like TN will be a big lesson for them,” Manav told TOI after the end of a practice session on Saturday.Manav, who played three Test matches for Team India with exceptional success, is confident of putting up a fine show. “Our team also has experienced players like Mahipal Lomror (vice-captain) and left-arm spinner Ajay Kookna. Their presence will certainly help. Kartik Sharma and Mukul Choudhary also have IPL experience with them. We should do well,” said Manav, who captained the side in white ball cricket last season.The visitors also have several U-23 players in the squad. “We won the U-23 national title last season. The top performers have been given a chance in the senior side now. They will be eager to perform at this level too,” Sai Kishore told reporters on the eve of the match.SquadsRajasthan: Manav Suthar (captain), Mahipal Lomror (vice-captain), Rohan Rajbar, Sachin Yadav, Sumit Godara, Kartik Sharma, Karan Lamba, Anshul Gadhwal, Mukul Choudhary (WK), Ajay Kookna, Aakash Singh, Chetan Sharma, Hemant Choudhary, Danish Bhamboo, Darshan Jain (WK).Tamil Nadu: R Sai Kishore (captain), C Andre Siddarth, N Jagadeesan, G Ajitesh, B Indrajith, Pradosh Ranjan Paul, Nidhish S Rajagopal, SR Athish, R Vimal Khumar, S Ajith Ram, J Hemchudeshan, P Saravana Kumar, R Sonu Yadav, Esakkimuthu, D Deepesh, G Govinth, Washington Sundar.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: ‘ Mohammed Shami bhi aa rahe hai piche piche’: Suresh Raina drops big hint on India pacer’s return
articles.summary: Former India cricketer Suresh Raina believes Mohammed Shami could soon return to the national team, following the comeback of his former teammate
articles.body: Former India cricketer Suresh Raina believes Mohammed Shami could soon return to the national team, following the comeback of his former teammate Bhuvneshwar Kumar, who has earned a recall at the age of 36.Raina credited Bhuvneshwar’s discipline, hard work and commitment to his fitness for his return to the Indian side, expressing confidence that Shami could also be back in contention after making an impact in domestic cricket.“Making it to the Indian team at the age of 36 shows character. He has been a very disciplined bowler and a very process-driven guy who has worked really hard on his body," Raina said while speaking at the jersey launch of the Indian Soft Ball Cricket League.Raina was equally optimistic about Shami’s prospects, pointing to his performances in domestic cricket and suggesting that a return to the national team could be around the corner.“Absolutely, I think he (Mohammed Shami) has done well and played good domestic cricket too. Now it is Bhuvi’s turn, aur Shami bhi aa rahe hai piche piche, tension mat lijiye (Shami is also right behind him, so don’t worry)," Raina added.Shami last featured for India during the 2025 Champions Trophy, while his most recent appearance in Test cricket came in the 2023 World Test Championship final against Australia. Since then, the fast bowler has continued to play domestic cricket and is set to represent Bengal in their opening fixture of the 2026-27 Ranji Trophy season.However, his recent IPL numbers have been a concern. Shami has managed just 18 wickets in 22 matches across the 2025 and 2026 seasons, conceding runs at an economy rate of 10 per over.Bhuvneshwar, meanwhile, has demonstrated how skill and precision can compensate for a lack of outright pace in the shortest format. Although his gentle pace might appear to put him at a disadvantage, particularly on flat pitches, his ability to swing the new ball and execute variations at the death has helped him remain effective.The right-arm pacer was particularly effective in the PowerPlay and death overs, claiming 25 wickets in overs 1-6 and another 18 in overs 16-20 across the 2025 and 2026 IPL seasons.Bhuvneshwar took his game to another level in IPL 2026, finishing as the second-highest wicket-taker with 28 scalps at an economy rate of 8.07. He was one of the key figures in Royal Challengers Bengaluru’s title-winning campaign, helping the franchise secure back-to-back titles.Those figures put Bhuvneshwar ahead of Josh Hazlewood, Jofra Archer and Mohammed Siraj in the two key phases of the innings, underlining the value of his control and experience.His return to the Indian team has also offered a reminder that sustained discipline and an understanding of a bowler’s role can keep the door open to international cricket. articles.title: India lose half their bowling strength without Jasprit Bumrah? Numbers reveal startling truth
articles.summary: India’s bowling numbers against Full Member teams in T20Is in 2026 tell a striking story: the difference Jasprit Bumrah makes to the attack is enormous,
articles.body: India’s bowling numbers against Full Member teams in T20Is in 2026 tell a striking story: the difference Jasprit Bumrah makes to the attack is enormous, and his absence leaves the team significantly more vulnerable.With Bumrah in the playing XI, India have claimed 111 wickets in 15 matches at an average of 22.18 and an economy rate of 8.77. In the 13 matches without their premier fast bowler, the numbers have taken a sharp dip, with India managing just 73 wickets at an average of 29.32 and conceding runs at 9.37 per over.The contrast underlines how heavily India rely on Bumrah to provide control and breakthroughs, particularly when opposition batters are looking to dominate. Without him, India have taken nearly half as many wickets despite playing almost as many matches, while their bowling average has deteriorated considerably.The figures assume even greater significance as India prepare for another high-scoring contest against the West Indies in Indore. The first two T20Is have exposed the difficulties faced by both bowling attacks on batting-friendly surfaces, with India winning in Lucknow before the visitors levelled the series in Ranchi.Shreyas Iyer's unbeaten 102 powered India to an eight-wicket win in Lucknow, but Shai Hope responded with an unbeaten century in Ranchi as West Indies chased down a mammoth 250 to level the series. The visitors showed they could overcome early setbacks, losing three wickets inside the PowerPlay before completing the chase.The challenge for India's bowlers is unlikely to ease in Indore, where small boundaries and a reputation for high scores could leave little room for error. articles.title: Matt Renshaw breaks Virat Kohli’s decade-old record with stunning 190 in Durban
articles.summary: Matt Renshaw has bettered a record held by Virat Kohli for nearly a decade, becoming the highest scorer while batting alongside the tail in a Test innings
articles.body: Matt Renshaw has bettered a record held by Virat Kohli for nearly a decade, becoming the highest scorer while batting alongside the tail in a Test innings since 2002.The Australian batter scored 174 runs in partnerships with the lower order during his career-best 190 against South Africa in the ongoing Test at Durban, going past Kohli’s previous benchmark of 171. Kohli had achieved the feat during his monumental 235 against England at Mumbai’s Wankhede Stadium in 2016.Renshaw’s contribution with the tail proved instrumental in Australia’s recovery after they slumped to 124/6. He added 41 runs in an 86-run stand with captain Pat Cummins, followed by 12 in a 20-run partnership with Mitchell Starc. His most significant contribution came alongside Nathan Lyon, with the pair putting on 134 runs for the ninth wicket, of which Renshaw scored 100. He then added another 21 in a 26-run stand with Josh Hazlewood.The partnerships helped Australia recover from a precarious position to finish their first innings at 390 all out on Day 2 at Kingsmead on Sunday.Renshaw faced 397 deliveries in his marathon innings, hitting 21 fours and a six. He fell just short of a maiden Test double century when Simon Harmer dismissed him, bringing an end to an innings that had transformed Australia’s fortunes.Cummins chipped in with 43, while Lyon made 27 off 92 balls to provide crucial support. For South Africa, Wiaan Mulder was the leading wicket-taker with 4/68, while Marco Jansen claimed three wickets and Anrich Nortje took two.Renshaw’s knock also established two significant milestones at the Durban venue. His 190 became the highest individual score by an Australian there, overtaking Phillip Hughes’ 160 in 2009. It was also the highest Test score at the ground by a batter coming in at No. 5 or lower, surpassing Kusal Perera’s unbeaten 153 in 2019.South Africa reached 27/1 by stumps in reply to Australia’s total, leaving them 363 runs behind. Josh Hazlewood provided the breakthrough by dismissing Ryan Rickelton for a duck, while Aiden Markram, unbeaten on 15, and David Bedingham, on 12, remained at the crease when bad light brought an early close to play.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.body: New Zealand are considering a new role for explosive batter Finn Allen in the upcoming ODI series against India, with head coach Rob Walter keen to test him in the middle order ahead of the next World Cup. Allen, who usually opens in T20 cricket, could be used to attack spinners and part-time bowlers during the middle overs."We've got a different role in mind for Finn in the middle order. So we want to explore that as an option, obviously given his capability to influence the game," Walter said, as quoted by PTI, during a virtual media interaction.He explained that the team wants a batter who can change the pace of the game between overs 25 and 40, particularly when batting conditions are favourable."We actually want to see what it looks like to have someone in the middle order just taking on the game," he said.New Zealand will play five T20Is and five ODIs against India, followed by a two-match Test series. The matches will help the team test different combinations and prepare for future international assignments.Fast-bowling workload remains a concernWalter said New Zealand are carefully managing their fast bowlers ahead of a busy schedule. Will O'Rourke is gradually returning after a lower-back injury, while Ben Sears is recovering from ankle surgery."The injury is sort of recovered and we're pretty happy with that, but there's obviously just a real safe loading pattern for him to get into to be ready for Test match cricket," Walter said about O'Rourke.The team hopes O'Rourke will be available for the Test series against Australia. Sears is expected to start running soon before gradually returning to bowling.Lockie Ferguson will feature only in the final two ODIs against India as part of the workload-management plan."He is desperate to play and he's made no bones about that, which is awesome. I love that. But it's also just taking the right steps to the process because a number of other guys have been playing in the meantime and doing well."Youngsters and coaching changesWalter also highlighted the value of New Zealand A players facing India A to gain experience against strong opposition.New Zealand have appointed former wicketkeeper-batter BJ Watling as batting coach, a move Walter believes will strengthen the team."He has a massive amount of respect already in the change room before having said a word," Walter said."I'm exceptionally excited by what he can bring to the group."Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.summary: Rahmat Shah made history on his first outing as Afghanistan’s Test captain, scoring a century against Bangladesh in the one-off Test at the Sheikh Zayed
articles.body: Rahmat Shah made history on his first outing as Afghanistan’s Test captain, scoring a century against Bangladesh in the one-off Test at the Sheikh Zayed Stadium in Abu Dhabi on Sunday. His 105-run knock made him the first Afghan cricketer to score a hundred on his Test captaincy debut.Shah, who took over as Afghanistan’s Test and ODI captain from Hashmatullah Shahidi in July, faced 216 balls and struck 10 fours and two sixes. However, his effort was not enough to prevent Afghanistan from falling behind Bangladesh in the first innings.After Bangladesh posted 346 runs, Afghanistan were bowled out for 240, giving their opponents a 106-run lead. Opener Abdul Malik contributed 62 off 120 balls, while wicketkeeper-batter Ikram Alikhil scored 32 from 103 deliveries. Shah remained the mainstay of the innings as the other batters struggled against Bangladesh’s bowling attack.Hasan Mahmud creates history with hat-TrickBangladesh fast bowler Hasan Mahmud delivered an outstanding performance, taking a hat-trick and finishing with five wickets. He became the first Bangladesh fast bowler to achieve a Test hat-trick and only the third player from the country to reach the milestone.Before Mahmud, Alok Kapali took a hat-trick against Pakistan in 2003, while Sohag Gazi achieved the feat against New Zealand in 2013.Mahmud also reached 50 Test wickets during the innings, becoming the fastest Bangladesh fast bowler to reach the milestone. He dismissed Yamin Ahmadzai, who was out for a duck, to complete his five-wicket haul. Fellow pacer Ebadot Hossain also played a key role, taking four wickets as Afghanistan were dismissed for 240.Bangladesh build strong first-innings totalEarlier, Bangladesh scored 346 in their first innings, with Tanzid Hasan Tamim leading the way with 83 runs.
