articles.title: Sobhana Mostary scripts history, becomes first Bangladesh woman to score century against Australia
articles.summary: Sobhana Mostary produced a record-breaking performance as Bangladesh recovered from a disastrous start to post 220/6 against Australia in the second ODI
articles.body: Sobhana Mostary produced a record-breaking performance as Bangladesh recovered from a disastrous start to post 220/6 against Australia in the second ODI at Allan Border Field. The right-handed batter struck her maiden international century, becoming the first Bangladesh woman to score an international hundred against Australia.Mostary's 118 off 134 balls proved crucial for the visitors after Australia elected to bowl first in the must-win encounter. Her fighting knock, combined with a valuable contribution from captain Nigar Sultana, helped Bangladesh recover from 8/3 and give themselves a competitive total.Mostary, Sultana rescue Bangladesh after early collapseBangladesh were in deep trouble early in their innings, losing three wickets for just eight runs. However, Mostary and Sultana joined forces to turn the game around, stitching together a remarkable 195-run partnership for the fourth wicket.Mostary showcased composure and determination throughout her innings, striking 18 boundaries to bring up a memorable century. Sultana provided equally important support, scoring 74 off 114 deliveries as the pair steadied the innings and laid the foundation for Bangladesh's recovery.Before Mostary's century, Sultana held the record for the highest individual score by a Bangladesh woman against Australia, having scored an unbeaten 63 in a T20I.Record-breaking partnership rewrites ODI historyThe 195-run stand between Mostary and Sultana became Bangladesh's highest partnership for any wicket in women's ODI cricket. The duo surpassed the previous record of 152 runs, which Sultana and Sharmin Akhter had registered for the third wicket against Thailand in 2025.The partnership also established a new benchmark against Australia in women's ODIs, eclipsing the previous record of 170 runs. New Zealand's Emily Drumm and Rebecca Rolls had held that record with their second-wicket stand in 2002.Mostary's landmark innings ended in the 48th over when Megan Schutt bowled her for 118. Schutt finished with four wickets, having struck twice in the powerplay to dismiss Fargana Hoque and Sharmin Akhter before later removing Shorna Akter.Bangladesh aim to level the seriesDespite the early setbacks, Bangladesh showed resilience to finish at 220/6, with Mostary and Sultana's record partnership providing the backbone of their innings. articles.title: ‘Serving a hungry lion a goat on a platter’: Ashwin explains how Shai Hope helped Sanju Samson regain form
articles.summary: Former India spinner Ravichandran Ashwin has questioned Shai Hope’s bowling decisions during the second T20I against India, arguing that the West Indies
articles.body: Former India spinner Ravichandran Ashwin has questioned Shai Hope’s bowling decisions during the second T20I against India, arguing that the West Indies captain made a tactical error by persisting with Akeal Hosein despite the spinner being taken apart by Sanju Samson.India piled up 249/5 in 20 overs in Ranchi on Friday, with Samson smashing 82 off just 41 deliveries. West Indies, however, produced a stunning response with the bat, chasing down the target with nine balls to spare as Hope struck an unbeaten 102 off 45 balls to level the five-match series at 1-1.While India’s batting dominated the first half of the contest, Ashwin felt Hope missed an opportunity to contain Samson by continuing to use Hosein during the PowerPlay.The left-arm spinner conceded 46 runs in three overs, struggling to contain Samson, who punished him with two sixes and two fours in one over. Despite the batter’s aggressive approach, Hope gave Hosein three consecutive overs before eventually leaving him out of the attack for the remainder of the innings.Ashwin criticised the decision, saying the West Indies captain could not expect to build pressure by repeatedly using a spinner against a batter who was finding boundaries with ease.“Samson looked scratchy because he was not in a run-scoring phase. However, Shai Hope also made a mistake today. You cannot keep using spinners from one end in an attempt to build pressure on Sanju Samson. Bowling three consecutive overs from Akeal Hosein during the powerplay was like serving a hungry lion a goat on a platter. Samson simply took advantage of the opportunity and went after Akeal Hosein," said Ashwin on his YouTube channel, Ash Ki Baat.Ashwin also praised Samson's approach, highlighting his willingness to keep taking risks for the team despite the pressure surrounding his place in the side."It is not easy to maintain that attitude. It is human nature that when you are in danger and know that you might be dropped, self-preservation becomes the top priority. Yet, he continues to take risks for the team. And it is this great attitude of his that seems to be bringing him some luck as well. A catch went straight into a fielder's hands today, but he dropped it," he added.Despite the expensive spell, West Indies managed to turn the game around with a commanding batting display. Hope led the chase with an unbeaten century, helping the visitors overcome the pressure of pursuing a total close to 250. articles.body: Steve Smith added another milestone to his Test career on Sunday, overtaking England's Joe Root to become the most successful fielder in Test cricket history during the first Test between South Africa and Australia at Kingsmead in Durban.Smith reached the landmark on Day 3 when he caught David Bedingham off Pat Cummins' bowling. Batting on 49, Bedingham edged a hard, back-of-a-length delivery towards first slip. Smith dived to his left to complete the catch, dismissing the South African batter just one run short of his half-century.The catch took Smith's tally to 221 in Test cricket, moving him past Root's previous record of 220. Rahul Dravid is third on the all-time list with 210 catches, followed by Sri Lanka's Mahela Jayawardene with 205 and South Africa's Jacques Kallis with 200. articles.title: Australia v South Africa: Pace attack and Steve Smith put tourists in charge
articles.summary: The fearsome pace quartet and Steve Smith's brilliance serves as a reminder of Australia's quality as the tourists take charge against South Africa.
articles.body:
South Africa 284: Bedingham 49; Cummins 3-54

Australia's modern Test side remain a fascinating one to unpick.

Viewed by many in England as there for the taking in last winter's Ashes despite a 4-1 win, they are also labelled too old by many observers at home.

The victims of recent shock defeats by West Indies and Bangladesh, they are still unbeaten in their past nine Test series.

But while their struggling batting line-up was bailed out by Matt Renshaw across the first two days of the first Test in Durban, they took control over South Africa on day three in an all-too familiar way.

Nine years after they first appeared together as Australia's bowling quartet, Mitchell Starc, Josh Hazlewood, Pat Cummins and Nathan Lyon produced their latest relentless performance to dismiss South Africa for 284. There was even some magic from Steve Smith thrown in too.

Cummins took three wickets, Starc, Hazlewood and Lyon two apiece, in doing so brushing off any doubts about their effectiveness at the start of a run of Tests against the world Test champions, in-form New Zealand, India and England.

How Australia's quartet turned the screw on South Africa

At 82-1 in response to Australia's 390, South Africa appeared well in the Test on a relatively good surface.

Australia's bowlers searched for early swing and Aiden Markram and David Bedingham countered with a second-wicket partnership which progressed at almost 4.5 runs per over.

It was then, at the 20-over mark, captain Cummins reverted to Australia's tried and tested - Lyon one end, the quicks rotating at the other.

Having bowled 34% of their deliveries full in the first 20 overs, Starc, Hazlewood and Cummins dragged back their lengths. There were only 19 deliveries pitched fuller than six metres between the 20th and 60th overs.

With deliveries easy to hit scarce, Markram and Bedingham attempted forced back-foot drives and edged to slip for 37 and 49 respectively.

Wiaan Mulder was caught in two minds and bounced out by Cummins. Tristan Stubbs top-edged the Australia captain to fine leg.

In Australia's first innings, Renshaw, who ground out a superb 190, faced 52 deliveries pitched as short and played a pull or hook shot to four of them. He scored runs with only one of those shots - when he had 176 runs to his name and had faced 368 balls.

The contrast to Renshaw's application could not have been greater.

Six overs after Stubbs was caught, Marco Jansen, who had struck six fours in quickly reaching 26, also tried to pull Hazlewood off a fuller length and was tamely caught at mid-off.

The quality of the bowling and fact the Proteas are playing their first Test since November were other factors in South Africa's slide.

At the other end, off-spinner Lyon bowled 19 overs at less than three runs per over.

The 39-year-old had a more worn pitch to utilise than South Africa's spinners and found significantly more turn and threat.

He also had the sprawling Steve Smith to his advantage.

Both of Smith's catches off Lyon, first to dismiss Temba Bavuma and then Kyle Verreynne, were feats of anticipation. He saw both right-handers shape to reverse sweep, gambled and clung on at close range. The first was good. The one-handed second was spectacular.

"He's an absolute freak," said Lyon. "He practices that in training.

"He is an incredible thinker of the game but the way he moves, premeditates, for those types of catches.

"There are not many people in the dressing room that would be able to pull off those two catches."

In between, Smith's leaping catch at second slip after Cummins found Bedingham's edge took the 37-year-old back above Joe Root as the non-wicketkeeper with the most catches in Test history on 223.

While he ended the day with three more catches than Root, he still has a catch percentage about 77%, which sits below the format average.

He creates, and occasionally drops, chances such as these - chances others would not have created.

The result is Australia's fabled foursome now have 607 wickets in Tests in which they have played as a quartet.

The next most successful bowling four-pronged attack is James Anderson, Stuart Broad, Ben Stokes and Moeen Ali, who took 415 wickets in their 31 Tests together for England.

"Each of these players will go down as a legend of Australian cricket," said former Australia bowler Jason Gillespie on ABC Radio.

"Starc got hit for a few early but I didn't mind that.

"Hazlewood was very good, as he always is. Cummins was hostile. He looked fresh."

Much has been made of Australia's ageing side and a perceived lack of succession planning.

At 37, Starc is the oldest of the three quicks but his average pace of 141.21km/h in 2026 is higher than any of his past three years. He is also averaging his most swing in a calendar year since 2015.

The concern for Australia comes when they are not fit, with Hazlewood having missed all five of last winter's Ashes Tests and Cummins four.

Australia's issue right now is keeping each of their quartet on the field, because they appear as good as ever.

At 33-0, Australia lead South Africa by 139 runs.

Even with bad light halting play early again, they should have the time to press home an advantage across the Test's final two days.

articles.title: From Irani heroics to Ranji rescue act: R Smaran keeps his run going with another big knock
articles.summary: VIJAYAWADA: For someone knocking on the doors of the Indian team, R Smaran had a modest start to the season.
articles.body: VIJAYAWADA: For someone knocking on the doors of the Indian team, R Smaran had a modest start to the season. He managed 82 runs in three innings for South Zone in the Duleep Trophy, but found his rhythm while representing Rest of India against Jammu and Kashmir in the Irani Cup. He scored a crucial 68 before following it up with a match-winning 135 in Srinagar earlier this month.On Sunday, the 23-year-old carried that form into Karnataka’s Ranji Trophy opener against Andhra. The added responsibility of leading the side in Devdutt Padikkal’s absence, in only his third season, did little to unsettle him.As established stars in the Karnataka line-up made an early beeline for the dressing room, Smaran appeared unperturbed, batting in his own zone. His well-crafted 126 pulled the former champions out of a hole after they had slumped to 9/3.“I think I’ve been batting really well. Obviously, the situation was that we were in a bit of a bother with four wickets down. After that, it was a matter of stretching our partnership. The mindset was always to play positive cricket and keep the scoreboard ticking,” Smaran said, reflecting on how he carried his Irani Cup momentum into the new season.He was quick to credit wicketkeeper-batter KL Shrijith, whose aggressive approach helped shift the pressure back on Andhra.“A lot of credit goes to Shrijith, the way he came in and took the momentum away immediately. He got a few boundaries, and that straightaway put a lot of pressure on them, which made my job easier,” he said.Having set the tone for what he hopes will be a productive season, the left-hander has his sights on a personal milestone. He fell 50 runs short of the 1,000-run mark last season and is keen to cross it this time, though he insists he is not burdening himself with expectations.“I didn’t come in with any expectations. The only thing that was running in my mind was that I missed out on scoring 1,000 runs last season and what I could achieve this season. I’m taking it one game at a time and ensuring that I’m winning games for my team whenever I can contribute,” he said.For Smaran, however, individual milestones take a back seat to Karnataka’s larger ambition. In the previous season, the team lost to Jammu and Kashmir in the final.“We came very close to winning the Ranji Trophy last season. But second place is just not good enough. The wait still goes on to get our hands on the trophy. So, the focus remains on winning it,” he said.For inspiration, Smaran & Co need not look far. articles.summary: VIJAYAWADA: When stand-in skipper R Smaran walked out to bat, Karnataka were in disarray at 9/3.
articles.body: VIJAYAWADA: When stand-in skipper R Smaran walked out to bat, Karnataka were in disarray at 9/3. He briefly looked up at the blazing sun before making his way to the middle, where the early damage had left the visitors looking like a team caught in a storm.For the next 328 minutes, the 23-year-old held his ground, batting with purpose, precision and impressive game awareness to craft a 218-ball 126 (11x4; 1x6). With KL Shrijith (58; 82b; 3x4; 3x6) for company, the left-hander hauled the former champions out of deep trouble against Andhra with a mature and chanceless innings.At the ACA Stadium in Mulapadu, on the outskirts of Vijayawada, Karnataka, who opted to bat in their Ranji Trophy season opener on Sunday, recovered from a disastrous start to post 274 in 82.2 overs. The visitors, however, struck back before stumps, leaving Andhra precariously placed at 16/2 after five overs.The venue, nestled in the foothills of the Kondapalli Reserve Forest range and surrounded by the Eastern Ghats, drew a sizable crowd despite the searing heat. Many had turned up to watch Karnataka’s star-studded batting lineup, but the early movement on offer left the top order struggling to find its feet.Mayank Agarwal (5) was the first to go, losing his off stump to Kavuri Saiteja (2/20) after miscuing a short-of-good-length delivery. Karnataka needed to negotiate the first hour, but the batters appeared in a hurry. KV Aneesh fell the very next ball, poking at a delivery and offering Ricky Bhui a catch in the slips.KL Rahul (4) was expected to steady the innings but edged KV Sasikanth (2/10) to wicketkeeper Revanth Reddy. Karun Nair followed, trapped in front by an inswinger from Sasikanth.At 22/4, Karnataka were in serious trouble. Shrijith joined Smaran and the pair offered contrasting approaches. Shrijith took the attack to Andhra with reverse sweeps and pulls, while Smaran, who had opened his account with a crisp back-foot punch through point, focused on finding gaps and rotating the strike.Their 111-run stand for the fifth wicket eased the pressure before left-arm spinner Saurabh Kumar (3/69) broke the partnership. articles.title: South Africa vs Australia: Pat Cummins, Mitchell Starc, Nathan Lyon among wickets as Baggy Greens take command of first Test in Durban
articles.summary: Australia hold a commanding 139-run lead against South Africa in Durban after the hosts were bowled out for 284 on day three; watch day four of the first Test live on Sky Sports Cricket on Monday, with coverage starting from 8:30am
articles.body:
A collective bowling effort from Australia saw South Africa bowled out for 284 in their first innings, with Mitchell Starc (2-63), Josh Hazlewood (2-54) and Nathan Lyon (2-58) also among the wickets.

Australia scored 390 runs in their first innings with Matt Renshaw hitting a career-best 190 to help the visitors recover from a precarious 124-6.

In their second innings, Australia were 33-0 at stumps from 5.4 overs - Nic Maddinson 17no and Travis Head 10no - when play was called off early again due to bad light, with nearly 13 overs lost in the day.

David Bedingham top-scored for South Africa with 49 off 73 balls. The hosts were 197-8 at one stage before a 52-run ninth-wicket partnership between Keshav Maharaj (34) and Simon Harmer (35no) repaired some of the damage.

South Africa are the reigning world Test champions and beat Australia in the 2025 final. It is Australia's first trip to the country since the 2018 ball-tampering scandal when they last toured there.

Australia bowlers make difference on day three

South Africa were down to 115-4 at lunch. Starting from 27-1 on day two, Aiden Markram (37) and Bedingham added 57 runs to their overnight partnership.

The breakthrough for Australia came just before drinks when Markram edged Starc to slip in the 21st over.

South Africa scored 59-1 in the first hour. In the second hour, Temba Bavuma (3) was out caught off Lyon - Steve Smith taking a well-judged catch as Bavuma went for a reverse sweep.

Cummins then had Bedingham caught in the slips with Smith taking another great catch to his left.

After lunch, Cummins struck again. Wiaan Mulder was the first to go - he scored 30 off 50 balls with three fours and a six, adding 56 with Tristan Stubbs.

Stubbs fell soon after for 32 - caught at square leg, again off Cummins.

Lyon had Kyle Verreynne caught at slip for 13 as South Africa stumbled to 197-7. Marco Jansen hit six fours for a 20-ball 26, before holing out off Hazlewood.

South Africa were 238-8 at tea with Harmer and Maharaj able to go past the follow-on mark. Their 50-partnership ended when Starc dismissed Maharaj.

articles.title: Abhishek's blitz, Arshdeep's strikes help India beat West Indies by 14 runs in Indore, take 2-1 lead in T20I series
articles.summary: INDORE: A brilliant bowling display by India on a flat pitch with shorter boundaries at the Holkar Stadium guided them to a 14-run win over the West
articles.body: INDORE: A brilliant bowling display by India on a flat pitch with shorter boundaries at the Holkar Stadium guided them to a 14-run win over the West Indies and gave them a 2-1 lead in the series on Sunday.With dew not coming into play in the third T20I, India's bowlers showcased their capabilities when the contest between bat and ball was evenly poised. They were on the money on most occasions, executed their plans perfectly and did not get rattled when the West Indies batters threatened to take the game away. In the end, the visitors were restricted to 209/7 while chasing a target of 224.It began up front when Mayank Yadav (0/34) bowled all his deliveries above 145 kmph, hurrying the batters and conceding just two runs in his opening over. In the next over, West Indies skipper Shai Hope (5, 5b; 1x4) tried to force the pace but was cleaned up by Arshdeep Singh (3/44).The West Indies then settled into a nice rhythm. They were not scoring at the rate India had managed in the Powerplay, but were doing enough to stay within touching distance of the required rate. Their charge was led by Shimron Hetmyer (43, 26b; 6x4, 2x6), who took the attack to the Indian bowlers. The left-hander had just taken 10 runs off two balls in the seventh over bowled by Naman Dhir (2/39), but on the very next delivery the off-spinner bowled a quicker ball with a flat trajectory that skidded on and rattled the stumps.The dismissal stalled the visitors' scoring rate and they needed regular boundaries to stay in touch with the chase. Rovman Powell (5, 7b), who was struggling to get going, tried to force the issue but could only hit an Axar Patel (1/33) delivery straight down the throat of Ishan Kishan at deep mid-wicket. In the next over, Kamil Pooran (42, 27b; 3x4, 3x6) hit Dhir for three sixes before the Punjab all-rounder had him caught in the deep.India then bowled a series of tight overs through Prince Yadav (0/37), Nitish Kumar Reddy (1/19) and Arshdeep, pushing the required rate up to 15 an over. The visitors gave it their all, but the target ultimately proved too steep.Earlier, India were bowled out for 223 and owed much to the 108-run second-wicket partnership between Abhishek Sharma (69, 30b; 6x4, 5x6) and Ishan Kishan (37 18b; 6x4, 1x6), which came off just 40 deliveries and laid the platform for a total beyond 200.Uncertain about whether dew would come into play, India could not afford to take their foot off the pedal. However, in their attempt to keep the scoring rate as high as possible, they lost their way through the middle overs. Perhaps memories of the West Indies chasing down 250 in the previous game weighed heavily on their minds after being put in to bat.India managed just seven runs in the first two overs, with Sanju Samson (3, 6b) already back in the pavilion. But the floodgates opened thereafter as they added 80 runs in the next four overs to finish the Powerplay at 87/1. At one stage, they were cruising at 115/1 after 8.1 overs, with Abhishek and Ishan dispatching the West Indies bowlers all around the park.Then came the twist that knocked the wind out of India's innings. The visitors tightened the screws, taking four wickets in the space of 16 balls to claw their way back into the contest.As in the previous match, Roston Chase (2/38) used his cricketing nous to spark the fightback with two wickets in the ninth over. He first had Kishan stumped, a ball after being hit for a six, to end the pair's 108-run partnership. Two deliveries later, the off-spinner trapped skipper Shreyas Iyer lbw as the Indian captain looked to maintain the brisk scoring rate.Five balls later, it was Abhishek's turn to depart after the left-hander skyed a short-of-a-length delivery from Shamar Springer (2/50). Naman Dhir (10, 5b; 1x4, 1x6) looked promising, launching Gudakesh Motie (1/37) over mid-on for six, but the left-arm spinner had the last laugh two balls later as the right-hander holed out at long-off.India were suddenly reduced to 135/5 after 10.5 overs.
